chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked him about a man who forgot the Dhuhr prayer until the time for Asr entered. He said: 'He should begin with Dhuhr; and similarly, the prayers should begin with that which you forgot, unless you fear that the time for the prayer will expire, so you should begin with that which is currently within its time, then pray that which you forgot.'
ai.seo_question: What is the correct order of prayers if one misses Dhuhr and realizes it during Asr time?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of prioritizing the 'time of fear' (khawf al-fawt) over the general order of prayers, ensuring that the obligatory prayer currently in its valid window is not missed. It reflects the practical application of maintaining the integrity of daily worship by balancing the obligation of making up missed prayers (qada) with the urgency of current ones, a nuance often discussed in Usul al-Fiqh regarding the sequence of acts of worship.
